items.title: T Market is opening its Massachusetts flagship at Natick Mall
items.description: T Market lists an August 27 grand opening ceremony for its Massachusetts flagship at Natick Mall. The store combines grocery, Asian beauty, a food hall and bakery, and the company publicly lists a purchasing contact. That creates an unusually direct prospecting signal without proving that any specific purchase is currently open.
why: Public purchasing contact is listed by the company

items.title: Maersk is opening a 617,000-square-foot fulfillment hub in Hopedale
items.description: Maersk says its new $100 million Hopedale fulfillment hub will begin operations in late August 2026, create approximately 1,000 jobs and support high-volume e-commerce fulfillment. The scale and near-term launch make this a strong operating-services signal, but no specific local vendor request is stated.

items.title: 42 North Dental is opening its new Boston home office on August 26
items.description: 42 North Dental is moving its home office from Waltham to 99 Summer Street in Boston and lists August 26 as the date its new Hub will be open and ready for team members. The move creates a near-term workplace and facility-support signal without evidence of a specific open purchasing request.

items.title: Big Y is preparing to open a new Saugus supermarket
items.description: Big Y lists Saugus among its grand-opening locations, with a September 10 opening date reported for the approximately 46,000-square-foot supermarket. The company has also been hiring heavily for the site, making this a strong pre-opening operations signal rather than a confirmed vendor request.

items.title: HomeGoods is opening its relocated Acton store on August 27
items.description: HomeGoods lists an August 27 opening for its relocated Acton store at The Shops at Highland Commons. A retail relocation creates a timely prospecting signal for move-in, facilities and local operating services, though no specific vendor request is stated.

items.title: Hawksmoor is opening a 200-seat Boston restaurant on September 8
items.description: Hawksmoor says its first Boston restaurant will open September 8 in Fort Point with space for around 200 guests and a large outdoor terrace. The imminent full-service restaurant launch creates plausible recurring operating and facility-service needs, but no specific vendor solicitation is stated.

items.title: SMC is expanding its Devens medical-device manufacturing campus
items.description: Massachusetts awarded SMC $1.25 million to renovate its existing 330,000-square-foot Devens facility and construct a new 100,000-square-foot building. The project is expected to create 190 jobs and includes HVAC, power, injection-molding and building-system work. This is a strong expansion signal, not a confirmed open vendor request.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Walmart won approval for a new Newton microfulfillment facility
items.description: Newton's Zoning Board of Appeals approved a variance allowing Walmart to move forward with an approximately 20,000-square-foot microfulfillment center in Auburndale. The project creates a future site-services signal rather than a confirmed vendor request.
why: Fulfillment operations can create recurring site-service needs

items.title: Autonodyne is building an autonomy demonstration and training center in Boston
items.description: Massachusetts awarded Autonodyne $1 million for construction and equipment for a 6,500-square-foot autonomy demonstration center with simulator stations, secure collaboration space, IT systems and training areas. The state says the company anticipates sourcing most project work from Massachusetts-based vendors.
why: Project includes IT, simulator and training infrastructure
Company anticipates sourcing most project work from Massachusetts vendors
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Helfrich Bros. plans a new 65,000-square-foot Lawrence manufacturing facility
items.description: Massachusetts awarded Helfrich Bros. $1 million to help acquire adjacent land and construct a new 65,000-square-foot manufacturing facility with cranes, welding equipment, an automated paint booth and a testing station. The project is expected to create at least 30 jobs and support local suppliers.
why: State announcement notes support for local suppliers
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Wonder is scheduled to open a Brookline location on August 27
items.description: Wonder's published regional expansion schedule lists a Brookline opening for August 27. The food-service opening creates a near-term prospecting signal for recurring operating and facility vendors, although vendor demand is not confirmed.

items.title: Zealand Pharma is preparing a new U.S. research hub in Cambridge
items.description: Zealand Pharma is preparing a Cambridge research hub that is expected to become operational in September 2026 and serve as its primary U.S. address. The lab-focused site is intended to support AI-driven drug discovery, automation and research expansion, creating plausible technical and facility-service needs without evidence of a specific open vendor request.

items.title: Babilou Family US is opening an early-education center in Allston in September
items.description: Babilou Family US says its new infant-through-pre-K center at the Enterprise Research Campus in Allston will open in September 2026. A new childcare facility can create recurring facility, janitorial, security and operating-supply needs, but no purchasing request is stated.
why: Recurring facility and operating needs are plausible

items.title: Boston Dynamics is developing a 330,000-square-foot Waltham robotics center
items.description: Massachusetts says a Business Builds award will support renovation and buildout of approximately 330,000 square feet in Waltham for robotics manufacturing, training, R&D and related operations. The project supports plans for 650 new full-time jobs over three years.
why: 650 planned new jobs over three years
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: CBSET is relocating and expanding into a 104,000-square-foot Waltham facility
items.description: Massachusetts awarded CBSET $1 million to support relocation from Lexington to Waltham and renovation of a 104,000-square-foot building with laboratories, procedure rooms, operating rooms, offices and upgraded building controls. The project is expected to create 75 jobs over three years.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development
